title: Blindfold: Keeping the Audit Coin Secret from LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.37055v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Audit-based certification bounds the violation rate of an LLM agent by auditing a random fraction $\varepsilon$ of actions and reweighting the audited labels; its validity is meant to rest only on the defender's audit coin. We show that it also rests on a confidentiality property: the coin must not interfere with the agent's view before the action commits, at a time the agent chooses. We call this pre-commit noninterference (PNI) and measure its violation by $D_{\mathrm{A}}$, the total-variation distance between the agent's views under the two coin values. PNI is necessary and sufficient for an unbiased certificate against adaptive agents, the worst-case bias is $(1-\varepsilon)D_{\mathrm{A}}$, and no procedure that sees only audited labels can pay less. translated_title: Blindfold：对LLM智能体保密的审计硬币
translated_abstract: 基于审计的认证通过随机审计比例为 ε 的动作并对被审计的标签重新加权，来约束LLM智能体的违规率；其有效性本应仅取决于防御者的审计硬币。我们证明它还依赖于一个保密性属性：在动作提交之前、且在智能体自选的时刻，硬币不得干扰智能体的视图。我们将其称为“提交前不干扰”，并用 D_A——智能体在两种硬币取值下视图之间的总变差距离——来度量其违背程度。PNI 是对抗自适应智能体获得无偏证书的充分必要条件，最坏偏差为 (1-ε)D_A，且任何仅能观测被审计标签的程序都无法付出更小的代价。泄露会在步骤之间复合；跨回合共享的资源会开启一个大小可计算的信道；提高审计率也无法恢复有效性。在我们构建的一个监控器上，一个静默的……（原文此处截断）
tldr: 该论文揭示了基于审计的LLM智能体认证的有效性还依赖于“提交前不干扰”这一保密性属性，证明其充要性并给出最坏偏差 (1-ε)D_A，同时指出泄露会跨步骤复合且提高审计率也无法弥补失效。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that audit-based certification of LLM agents additionally relies on pre-commit noninterference (PNI)—the audit coin must stay secret from the agent before it commits an action—and proves PNI is necessary and sufficient for an unbiased certificate with worst-case bias (1-ε)D_A, while leakage composes across steps and higher audit rates cannot restore validity.
